# Background layers (Canvas → Popover)

**Figma:** Color/Background — Canvas · Surface · Container · Popover  
**Import:** `/* tokens */ var(--zen-color-background-canvas-default|alt|flat) · var(--zen-color-background-surface-default|alt|flat) · var(--zen-color-background-container) · var(--zen-color-background-popover-default)`

Every background sits on one of five layers, bottom to top: 1 Canvas (the page) · 2 Surface (containers on the page) · 3 other colours (component fills: subtle, solid, support) · 4 Container (Modal and Bottom-Sheet) · 5 Popover (floating overlays). Pick the token by the layer the box lives on, never by how it looks.

## Use it for
- Canvas — always the bottom layer: the page colour of the design. canvas-default is the norm; canvas-alt is for designs that want a white page.
- Surface — cards and containers placed on the Canvas. Choose surface-default or surface-alt to suit the style of the page (e.g. white cards on a canvas-default page; a softer surface-alt on a canvas-alt page). Canvas-alt and surface-default are the same colour, so a surface-default box on a canvas-alt page always gets a border (§11).
- Canvas-flat + Surface-flat — for flat designs: top and bottom navigation containers on a canvas-flat page use surface-flat, so the bar and the page read as one seamless surface in both light and dark mode.
- Other colours — component fills (Neutral/Subtle, Support/*, Solid, states) sit on Surface or Canvas.
- Container — only Modal/Dialog, Modal/Forms and Bottom-Sheet panels.
- Popover — the top layer: popovers, menus, dropdowns, tooltips, date pickers, flyouts, toasts.

## Use something else for
- Painting a component with Canvas — Canvas is the page, components start at Surface.
- Using Container for an in-page card, or Popover for an in-flow panel — both belong to floating layers.

## Figma → React
| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Canvas | `--zen-color-background-canvas-default · -alt · -flat` | page background (:root / app shell) |
| 2 Surface | `--zen-color-background-surface-default · -alt · -flat` | cards, panels, sidebars on the page; -flat = top/bottom navigation on a canvas-flat page |
| 3 Other colours | `--zen-color-background-<family>-<subtle|solid|pale>…` | component fills and states |
| 4 Container | `--zen-color-background-container` | Modal, Dialog, Modal/Forms, Bottom-Sheet |
| 5 Popover | `--zen-color-background-popover-default` | Popover, menus, tooltips, pickers, flyouts, toasts |

## ✅ Do
- On a canvas-alt (white) page, frame every surface-default card or panel with a closed border — 0 0 0 1px Border/Neutral/Pale when static, Subtle when actionable — or switch it to surface-alt (§11).
- Keep Subtle, Pale and Surface-Alt surfaces flat: separate them with a 0 0 0 1px ring or an inset effect, never a drop shadow (§9); guard component shadows with var(<background token>-shadow-off, `<shadow>`).
- Start every page with Canvas; choose default (most designs) or alt (white page).
- Place cards on the page with Surface; match default/alt to the page style.
- On a canvas-flat page, give top and bottom navigation surface-flat so both modes stay seamless.
- Only raise a box to Container or Popover when it actually floats above the page (modal, sheet, overlay).

## ❌ Don't
- Don't put a surface-default box on a canvas-alt page without a border — they are the same colour, and a shadow alone does not separate them (harness: layer/surface-on-canvas-alt-border).
- Don't cast a drop shadow from a Subtle, Pale or Surface-Alt background, even where Figma pairs one with Shadow/Action/* (harness: surface/no-shadow-on-tinted).
- Don't paint a card, panel or component with a Canvas token (harness: layer/canvas-is-page).
- Don't give the page (:root/html/body) a Surface or other token (harness: layer/root-is-canvas).
- Don't use surface-flat for cards; it is for navigation on a flat page (harness: layer/surface-flat-is-navigation).
- Don't use Background/Container outside Modal and Bottom-Sheet (harness: layer/container-is-modal).
- Don't use Background/Popover for in-flow content (harness: layer/popover-is-overlay).

## Accessibility
- Layer contrast is a cue, not the only one: floating layers also carry elevation (Effect/Container, Effect/Popover) and focus management.

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layer/root-is-canvas` | error | The page (:root / html / body) is layer 1 and paints a Canvas token: canvas-default (most designs), canvas-alt (white pages) or canvas-flat. | `zen-allow-root-background: <reason>` |
| `layer/canvas-is-page` | error | Canvas is only the page layer; components never paint Canvas — cards and containers on the page use Surface. | `zen-allow-canvas-layer: <reason>` |
| `layer/surface-flat-is-navigation` | warn | Surface/Flat is for top/bottom navigation containers on a Canvas/Flat page, so both modes read as one seamless surface. | `zen-allow-surface-flat: <reason>` |
| `surface/no-shadow-on-tinted` | error | A Subtle / Pale / Surface-Alt background never casts a drop shadow (inset effects and 0 0 0 Npx rings are fine); guard component shadows with <bg>-shadow-off. | `zen-allow-tinted-shadow: <reason>` |
| `layer/surface-on-canvas-alt-border` | error | Canvas/Alt and Surface/Default are the same colour: a Surface/Default box on a Canvas/Alt page needs a border (Pale if static, Subtle if actionable) — a shadow alone is not enough. | `zen-allow-surface-on-canvas-alt: <reason>` |
| `layer/container-is-modal` | warn | Background/Container (layer 4) is reserved for Modal and Bottom-Sheet panels. | `zen-allow-container-layer: <reason>` |
| `layer/popover-is-overlay` | warn | Background/Popover (layer 5, the top layer) is for floating overlays: popovers, menus, tooltips, pickers, flyouts, toasts. | `zen-allow-popover-layer: <reason>` |
